axes.model_access:
**Same origin as the Cursor editor: the model catalog follows the account.**

Example selectable models on the official CLI landing page:

- **Auto**
- **Composer 2**
- **Opus 4.6**
- **Codex 5.3 High Fast**
- **Gemini 3 Pro**
- **Grok**

The same page also says it covers:

- frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Cursor, etc.

The official model names (original English):

**Official landing-page wording**:
**Auto, Composer 2, Opus 4.6, Codex 5.3 High Fast, Gemini 3 Pro, Grok**

The models & pricing page lists another batch: Claude 4.6 Opus / Sonnet, Gemini 3.1 Pro,
GPT-5.3 Codex, GPT-5.4, Grok 4.20 and Composer 2.

Switch models via `--model <model>`, `--list-models`, `agent models`, `/model`.

**Enterprises can restrict available models via admin policies.** A restricted model passed to `--model`
exits with restriction info. Official CLI changelog wording:

**Official CLI changelog wording**:
"Admin Team model restrictions apply in the CLI"

v2026.09.28 fixed a pitfall.
`--model` could previously silently run a shorter base model.

**The only difference from `./cursor.md` is the entry point.** The model catalog does not change by form factor.
axes.runtime:
**A local terminal process; the command name is `agent`.**

The official install script puts it in `~/.local/bin`; native Windows uses PowerShell.
Auto-update is on by default; `agent update` upgrades manually.

The lifecycle is mainly bound to the terminal session. But the official docs offer several "detach from the terminal" paths (see background).

**Compared with the IDE form in `./cursor.md`, there are three differences.**
One is the interaction surface: here it is the terminal.
Two is scriptability.
Three is integration: `agent acp` can run the CLI as an ACP server,
on stdio, for custom clients to connect.
axes.local_files:
**Operates within the repo/workspace; Git worktrees can isolate changes.**

Specify the workspace with `--workspace <path>`.
Use `-w/--worktree [name]` to create a new worktree under `~/.cursor/worktrees/<reponame>/<name>`
(sharing retention rules with the editor).

**Writing to disk is tightened by default.** To land changes in scripts you need `--force` (or `--yolo`).
Official headless-page wording:

**Official headless-page wording**:
"Without `--force`, changes are only proposed, not applied"

Note the parameters page has a contradicting statement; both pages coexist:

**Official parameters-page wording**:
"Has access to all tools, including write and shell"

Rules are read from `.cursor/rules` and `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` at the project root.
Read/write scope is precisely controlled by permissions `Read(...)` / `Write(...)`.
axes.background:
**The terminal process ends with the session, but the official docs provide three "detach from the terminal" paths.**

One is Cloud Agent handoff.
Prefixing a message with `&` in a session lets you pick it up on web or mobile at cursor.com/agents.

**Official wording**:
"continue running while you're away"

Two is **persistent sessions**.
Start with `agent persist`, detach with `/detach`, reconnect with `agent persist attach`,
manage with `agent persist list` / `stop`.
This capability came in v2026.08.26; changelog wording:

**v2026.08.26 changelog wording**:
"Keep agents running after you disconnect"

Three is `agent worker`, officially described as starting a private cloud worker:

**Official wording**:
"a private cloud worker that runs agents in your environment"

**The execution-environment ownership and quota limits of each of the three paths are not spelled out separately on the official pages.**
axes.tools:
**The tool surface has three layers, all three verified.**

**Layer one: built-in tools.** Official using-page wording:

**Official using-page wording**:
"Agent has tools for file operations, searching, running shell commands, and
web access"

Within it, Shell Mode (`/shell`, aliases `/sh`, `/run`) runs commands in a login shell.

**Layer two: MCP.** The CLI automatically reads `mcp.json`:

**Official wording**:
"automatically detect and respect your `mcp.json`"

Locations are `.cursor/mcp.json` or `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, sharing the same servers with the editor.
There is also the `agent mcp` subcommand (`login` / `list` / `list-tools` / `enable` / `disable`)
and `--approve-mcps`.

**Layer three: ACP.** `agent acp` exposes an ACP server over stdio + JSON-RPC.

Extension mechanisms additionally include plugins (`--plugin-dir`, `/plugin`),
skills (pasteable as a custom mode) and `.cursor/rules`.
axes.context:
**Sessions are resumable, forkable, and compactable.**

Continue sessions with `--resume [chatId]`, `--continue`, `agent resume`, `agent ls`, `/resume`.
`/fork` forks the current session into a new one; `/rewind` jumps back to earlier messages.
Context compaction uses `/summarize` (alias `/compress`).

v2026.09.22 fixed a pitfall: earlier summaries could drop the latest request or the whole session.
Now the most recent user message is preserved verbatim.
If summarization fails or is aborted, the original session is kept.

Long-term context relies on rules and skills.
`.cursor/rules` and `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` load automatically.
`/goal` can set a long-term goal, officially marked "Rolling out".

**Where cross-session memory is stored is not explained on this page by the official docs.**
axes.permissions:
**The permission design is the finest-grained part of this form factor, with additional sudo credential protection.**

There are two config files: global `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, project-level
`<project>/.cursor/cli.json`.

Permission tokens come in five classes:

- `Shell(cmd)`
- `Read(path)`
- `Write(path)`
- `WebFetch(domain)`
- `Mcp(server:tool)`

Controlled via `permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny`; **deny takes precedence over allow**.

**By default, every terminal command requires approval.** Official using-page wording:

**Official using-page wording**:
"Before running terminal commands, CLI will ask you to approve (y) or reject (n)"

`--force` (alias `--yolo`) grants a pass.
The sandbox is controlled by `/sandbox` or `--sandbox enabled|disabled`;
the official docs say disabling uses "allowlist mode".

When `sudo` is needed, a masked password prompt appears. The official docs say the password goes straight to `sudo` via secure IPC:

**Official wording**:
"The AI model never sees it"

For CI, the official docs recommend **restricted autonomy + permission-based restrictions**,
writing instructions into `permissions.json` alongside Auto-review.
axes.fit:
Fits three kinds of people:

- those doing engineering tasks in the terminal, writing scripts, or running CI/CD (official GitHub Actions docs and cookbook)
- those already using Cursor who want the editor and terminal to share one account / models / MCP config
- those who need to hand sessions to a Cloud Agent or keep them running in a persistent session

**Not a fit** for scenarios requiring an open-source license.
Cursor CLI is a closed-source commercial product, requires a Cursor account or API key, and its usage is folded into the account's quota pool.

sections.与 IDE 形态的差异（本条目只写差异）:
| Dimension | Cursor (IDE form) | Cursor CLI (this entry) |
|---|---|---|
| Interaction surface | graphical editor | terminal process, command `agent` |
| Scripting | no native non-interactive entry | `-p / --print` + `--output-format text\|json\|stream-json` |
| CI | — | official GitHub Actions docs and cookbook |
| Editor integration | it is the editor | `agent acp` exposes an ACP server (stdio + JSON-RPC) |
| Shared items | account, models, `mcp.json`, `.cursor/rules`, quota pool | same |

**These are two installations of the same product.** The model catalog and quota pool do not change by form factor;
the differences are the interaction surface and degree of scriptability. See [Cursor](./cursor.md) (IDE form).
sections.headless / 非交互（本分区的关键点）:
The official headless page spells out the scripting contract:

- one-shot execution: `agent -p "..."`. Official wording "Use print mode (`-p, --print`) for
  non-interactive scripting and automation"

- landing changes: batch file edits need `--force` (alias `--yolo`). Official wording
  "Without `--force`, changes are only proposed, not applied"

- output: `--output-format text | json | stream-json`, with `--stream-partial-output` for incremental streaming; the example script parses `tool_call` events with `jq`

- auth: `export CURSOR_API_KEY=...` (stored as a repo/org secret in CI)
- trust: `--trust` trusts the workspace without interaction under headless

For CI, the official docs distinguish two autonomy levels and **recommend "restricted autonomy" for production**:
leave commits, pushes and comments to deterministic CI steps; the agent only edits files.
Then enforce hard constraints at the CLI layer via `permissions.allow` / `deny`.
sections.权限与沙箱:
Five permission-token classes, written in `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` (global)
or `<project>/.cursor/cli.json` (project-level). **deny takes precedence over allow**.

| token | example |
|---|---|
| `Shell(cmd)` | allow `Shell(git)`, deny `Shell(rm)` |
| `Read(path)` | `Read(**/*.md)`, deny `Read(.env*)` |
| `Write(path)` | `Write(src/**)`, deny `Write(**/*.key)` |
| `WebFetch(domain)` | fetches not in allow require approval each time |
| `Mcp(server:tool)` | `Mcp(datadog:*)`, `Mcp(*:*)` |

**In interactive mode, every terminal command requires approval by default.**
The sandbox toggles via `/sandbox` or `--sandbox enabled|disabled`; disabling degrades to allowlist mode.

When `sudo` is needed, the official docs say the password goes straight to `sudo` via secure IPC — **the model never sees it in plaintext**.
sections.变更记录要点（官方 CLI changelog）:
| Version | Key change |
|---|---|
| `v2026.09.28` | `--model` / `/model` now run the exact model you chose (previously could silently run a shorter base model) |
| `v2026.09.22` | Auto-review: decides whether MCP calls pass or are blocked per instructions in `permissions.json`; fixed summaries dropping requests |
| `v2026.08.26` | **persistent sessions**: `agent persist` keeps agents running after disconnect; team model restrictions take effect in the CLI |

The official docs have a dedicated **Cursor CLI changelog** page, separate from IDE / Agents Window / SDK.
`agent --version` shows the version; `agent update` upgrades in place.

**Suggested measurement**: focus on **the actual "no-write vs write" behavior in non-interactive mode**.
The two official pages disagree.
The headless page says: without `--force`, nothing lands on disk.
The parameters page says: the CLI has access to all tools, including write and shell.

This is the single best thing to verify with a real CI pipeline.

Second, test **the consistency of persistent sessions (`agent persist`) after network disconnects**.
